column3: It restates reliance upon God and His sufficiency as guardian, directly clarifying the focus command.

It joins God's full knowledge of deeds to their complete requital, specifying the focus's knowledge of servants' sins.
It almost exactly repeats God's sufficient knowledge of His servants' sins while placing it within historical destruction.
The servants' plea to be turned from Hell adds the ethical and punitive horizon for the focus's mention of their sins.
God's possession of all heavens and earth supplies a universal ground for calling Him sufficient as guardian.
It combines patience, seeking forgiveness for sin, and praise, closely extending the focus's praise before the Knower of sins.

The resurrection call answered with praise adds an eschatological dimension to the focus's praise of the Living One.

The repeated emergence of living from dead and dead from living supports the focus's mortality contrast.

Moses' fear over a particular offense does not clarify the focus's reliance or divine knowledge.

God as creator of all and guardian over everything broadens the focus's claim of sufficient guardianship.
It adds God's unceasing life, exhaustive knowledge, and effortless preservation, though the Living designation is already supplied.

God's causing death and life directly reinforces the contrast with the One who does not die.

God's superior knowledge, mercy or punishment, and the Prophet's non-guardianship sharpen the distinction in the focus.

The encompassing knowledge of all that belongs to a ruler reinforces the scope of divine informed oversight.

The challenge about reviving decayed bones clarifies human mortality against the focus's deathless Lord.

The Creator's extraction of living from dead and dead from living further supports the life-and-death contrast.
God's true judgment and hearing and seeing offer general grounds for reliance but do not add the focus's central terms.

Forgiveness of earlier and later sin adds a comprehensive forgiveness counterpart to divine awareness of sins.

The statement of humiliating punishment for disbelief gives only broad consequence context.

God's giving life and death and inheriting all supplies another basis for His enduring sovereignty.
The account of winds, clouds, and rain does not materially clarify the focus.
The assertion of witness without a clear subject or relation adds no usable clarification.
The immediate sequel identifies hostile criminals and God's sufficient guidance and help for the messenger.
The punishment scene in which death does not end suffering contrasts forcefully with reliance on the One who never dies.
The revival after a hundred years demonstrates divine power over death, supporting the focus's mortality contrast.
The command's arrival and God's transcendence give only a general praise-related context.
God's fuller knowledge of their speech and sufficient testimony reinforce His informed judgment of human claims.
The closing greeting upon the messengers does not clarify reliance, praise, or knowledge of sins.
Testing to disclose reports supplies a distant knowledge-of-deeds parallel, without the focus's devotional frame.
Formation in the womb and divine wisdom do not add a clear relation to the focus.
The unbelievers' Fire without death gives a final punitive contrast to the Ever-Living who never dies.
The prayer for pardon, forgiveness, mercy, and aid makes reliance an active petition under personal accountability.
The varied seizures of peoples because of their sins show accountable wrongdoing receiving fitting consequence.

God's sufficiency and best guardianship give a direct formula for the focus's reliance upon Him.
God's complete knowledge of enemies and sufficient guardianship and help reinforce informed reliance.

Believers' hearts tremble at God's mention and their reliance on their Lord portray the faithful response to His sovereignty.
It states that whoever relies on God finds Him mighty and wise, giving the rationale for trust.
It locates all affliction within what God has decreed and declares Him protector, supporting reliance amid uncertainty.
It joins God's sufficiency, unique divinity, and reliance upon the Lord of the mighty Throne.
Moses directs the believing community to place its reliance upon God if it has submitted.
Hud's reliance on God as Lord of all creatures grounds prophetic fearlessness in divine sovereignty.
Shu'ayb assigns success to God and declares reliance and return to Him, linking trust to prophetic action.
Jacob pairs God's decisive judgment with reliance on Him, clarifying trust without denial of practical means.

The messengers explicitly reason that they should rely on God because He has guided them through their paths.
Patience and reliance on the Lord are joined in the context of those who endure for God.
Satan has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord, showing the protective implication of trust.
All faces humble themselves before the Living, Self-Subsisting One, directly amplifying the focus's deathless Living Lord.

Every soul's tasting death establishes the universal creaturely mortality excluded by the focus.

The servants of the Merciful avoid idolatry, murder, and adultery, supplying the moral content behind divine knowledge of sins.
The multiplied enduring punishment of grave sin develops the accountability horizon surrounding the focus.
Repentance, faith, and righteous action lead God to replace evil deeds with good, directly answering the focus's mention of sins.
Everything perishes except God, supplying a forceful contrast to reliance on the One who does not die.
Every soul tastes death, reinforcing the creaturely mortality from which the focus distinguishes God.
Those who are patient and rely on their Lord combine endurance with the focus's commanded trust.
It declares God sufficient and directs those who rely to rely upon Him, directly restating the focus's trust rationale.
God takes souls at death and in sleep, clarifying His sovereignty over mortal life and death.
The throne-bearers glorify God with praise and seek forgiveness for believers, combining two central actions of the focus.
It assigns disputed judgment to God and explicitly joins reliance upon and turning back to Him.
Faithful support of the messenger is paired with glorifying and praising God morning and evening.
God's dominion includes giving life and death and encompasses all power, grounding the focus's deathless sovereignty.

Believers are directed to rely upon God when threatened by adversarial private counsel.
The Creator is named in exaltation and all that is in the heavens and earth glorifies Him, extending the focus's praise.
After affirming God's unique divinity, it commands believers to rely upon God directly.

God creates death and life as a test of deeds, connecting mortality and accountable action.
The believers affirm faith in the All-Merciful and reliance upon Him, directly parallel to the focus's command.
